cases.description: New route calls the model directly, bypassing the service layer

expected_violations.subject: app.routes.*
expected_violations.justification: HEAD code in routes/users.py already imports the model directly, and the new route continues the pattern. Structural predicate, reported at module level after module-level dedup.

expected_violations.subject: app.routes.*
expected_violations.justification: The new route writes user data without going through any service function.

expected_violations.subject: app.routes.*
expected_violations.justification: New API endpoint without any dependency on the centralized auth middleware.

cases.description: New service function uses the model: the sanctioned path

expected_violations.subject: app.routes.*
expected_violations.justification: Baseline only: pre-existing routes/users.py imports the model directly (marked '# violation' in the fixture). The new service function itself is compliant: services are the sanctioned path and requires app.models.* is satisfied via the call to User.find.

cases.grading_note: Any violation beyond the baseline prohibits would be a false positive: the service change itself must not trigger anything.

cases.description: New status endpoint with no auth middleware usage and no service dependency

expected_violations.subject: app.routes.*
expected_violations.justification: Baseline: pre-existing routes/users.py imports the model directly. The new status route touches no model.

expected_violations.subject: app.routes.*
expected_violations.justification: Per ADR-002 every API endpoint is authenticated unless under the /auth exemption, which covers login and token-refresh only. A status endpoint with no middleware dependency is a genuine violation.

cases.grading_note: requires app.services.* firing on status_route counts as a false positive: the ADR-001 rule is 'if a route needs data, it calls the service', and a data-less status endpoint needs no service. The middleware expectation currently scores as a miss: auth.py imports require_auth at module level and function-scope requires is satisfied by the enclosing module's imports (B2 fix tradeoff, #115). Per ADR-002 the endpoint is still unauthenticated (the decorator is not applied to status_route), so the expectation stays in the gold as a known miss.

cases.description: New endpoint in auth.py uses the service layer (layering compliant) but forgets the auth middleware: layering clean, auth violation

expected_violations.subject: app.routes.*
expected_violations.justification: Baseline only: pre-existing routes/users.py imports the model directly. The new route goes through the service layer and stays out of the model layer.

expected_violations.subject: app.routes.*
expected_violations.justification: whoami is an authenticated endpoint (the /auth exemption covers login and token-refresh only), and the new route has no dependency on the auth middleware.

cases.grading_note: The layering rules must stay quiet on this case: requires app.services.* must NOT fire because whoami_route calls get_user through the service layer. The middleware expectation currently scores as a miss: auth.py imports require_auth at module level and function-scope requires is satisfied by the enclosing module's imports (B2 fix tradeoff, #115). Per ADR-002 whoami is authenticated and the decorator is not applied, so the expectation stays in the gold as a known miss.

cases.description: New view calls the model directly, bypassing the service layer

expected_violations.subject: users.views.*
expected_violations.justification: The new view writes user data directly via User.objects.create without going through the service layer.

expected_violations.subject: users.views.*
expected_violations.justification: view handlers must not access data models directly: both the new create_user_view (User.objects.create) and the HEAD views (user_list, user_detail) use the model. Function-level subjects see the enclosing module's imports (B1 fix, #115), so the violation reports once at users.views.

cases.grading_note: The requires expectation must stay matched at create_user_view: views.py does not import users.services, so module-import seeding must not satisfy it.

cases.description: New view calls the service function, which itself uses the model: exercises the via-connector exemption

expected_violations.subject: users.views.*
expected_violations.justification: Baseline: HEAD user_list/user_detail access the model directly via the module-level import of users.models, reported once at users.views. The new delete_user_view itself must NOT be reported: its only path to the model goes through users.services.get_user, the sanctioned connector covered by users.services.* requires users.models.*.

cases.grading_note: A violation whose matched_fqn is users.views.delete_user_view would be a false positive: the via-connector exemption must keep the compliant view clean.

cases.description: Module-level assignment change in project/settings.py: no architectural impact

expected_violations.subject: users.views.*
expected_violations.justification: Baseline: HEAD users/views.py imports the model directly (user_list, user_detail use User), a diff-independent structural violation, consistent with the baseline expectations in the other django cases. The settings.py change itself is architecturally inert.

cases.grading_note: The settings.py change itself must produce no violation. project/urls.py transitively reaching users.models through users.views is not an ADR-002 violation: the ADR governs direct imports from the data model, and urls.py imports views only.

cases.description: New function in the serialization package: outside all constraint subjects, expect nothing
cases.grading_note: Zero violations expected: tuf.api.serialization is outside the tuf.api.metadata.* and tuf.repository.* subjects, and nothing in tuf depends on python2.7 or python3.5.

cases.description: New function in tuf/repository: module imports tuf.api.metadata, function-level reachability cannot see module imports
cases.grading_note: Zero violations expected: _repository.py already imports tuf.api.metadata at module level, so ADR-0010's requires is satisfied for function scope (enclosing-module seeding, #115). Any violation firing here is an over-trigger false positive.

cases.description: New function in tuf/ngclient: under tuf.* but outside the constrained subpackages, expect nothing
cases.grading_note: Zero violations expected: tuf.ngclient is under tuf.* (which only prohibits the dead Python versions) but outside tuf.api.metadata.* and tuf.repository.*.

cases.description: New code imports flask, violating ADR-0010 (flask replaced by django)

expected_violations.subject: openlobby.*
expected_violations.justification: New code imports flask after ADR-0010 replaced Flask with Django. Structural predicate, reported at the module that owns the new import.

cases.grading_note: requires violations on legacy_view (elasticsearch, django, django.db) count as false positives: openlobby/core/views.py already imports django at module level and satisfies ADR-0010's requires for function scope (enclosing-module seeding, #115). elasticsearch (ADR-0002's openlobby.core.* is over-broad for non-search functions) and django.db (views.py never imports django.db; ADR-0012's openlobby.* subject is over-broad) still over-trigger and remain recorded FPs. Only the flask prohibition is a true finding.

cases.description: Module-level assignment change in core/models.py: compliant, module-level imports keep django.db reachable
cases.grading_note: Zero violations expected: models.py imports django.db at module level (satisfying ADR-0010/0012 for openlobby.core.models.* and openlobby.*), and a module-level assignment is architecturally inert. ADR-0002 requires elasticsearch for openlobby.core.* firing here is a false positive: ADR-0002 is about fulltext search, not the data model.
